note: y
Not in the quotes:

Not in the quotes: “As the modelId”: citation 2’s text doesn’t show the field name modelId. “With Converse or InvokeModel”: only the Converse reference page is cited. InvokeModel is not quoted. “Inference profiles are used for cross-Region or application-level routing and cost tracking”: citation 1 covers cross-Region routing. “Application-level” and “cost tracking” are not in it.

Not in the quotes: “Than Geographic”: citation 3 is a stitched fragment, Global cross-Region inference | Approximately 10% savings, and leaves out the Cost | Standard pricing part. So nothing quoted says the savings are relative to Geographic. In docs-ai-004 the quote included “Standard pricing”, which is why that one was a y. “That is a difference in model pricing, not a routing fee”: this is the agent’s own interpretation, linking the two facts. It’s plausible given the “no additional routing cost” quote, but nothing quoted says it.
Geographic and global routing claims (within a geography like US/EU; any supported commercial Region) are not in any quote.

Not backed: the geographic-profile (within a geography like US or EU) and global-profile (any supported commercial Region) routing claims, the “Region you called the profile from” parenthetical, and “authoritative place to check”. It’s unsupported because neither citation contains any of that; both only say CloudTrail logs requests in the source Region and that additionalEventData.inferenceRegion shows where they were processed.

Not backed:“If a member account still gets AccessDeniedException, check that account’s status (e.g. with GetFoundationModelAvailability) and its IAM and AWS Marketplace permissions”: the troubleshooting advice isn’t in the quotes. Citation 3’s AccessDeniedException sentence ends in “contact AWS Sales”, a different instruction. GetFoundationModelAvailability appears in citation 2, but as a way to check status instead of waiting after submission, not as a fix for AccessDeniedException. Nothing quoted mentions IAM or Marketplace permissions as something to check.

Not backed:“Input JSONL files”: neither quote says JSONL. They say only “files you create” and that the input can be in InvokeModel or Converse format. JSONL is true of Bedrock batch inference, but it’s not in the evidence.

The recommendation and the Managed description are quoted, but the Customer-managed Knowledge Base name and its description (own RAG pipeline and vector store) are not in either quote, because both quotes end after the Managed bullet.

The scale-to-zero and cold-start claims are quoted, but the description of Provisioned Concurrency as keeping the endpoint warm for predictable bursts is not, because citation 1 ends right after naming the feature.

The headline “No” and the AsyncInferenceConfig requirement are quoted, but the InvokeEndpointAsync API name, the CreateEndpointConfig API name, and the advice to use a separate real-time endpoint are not in either quote.

The 80 tps default and the 100 tps burst limit are quoted, but the 80 concurrent requests, the ThrottlingException with HTTP 400, and the claim that the quota can be raised by a quota increase request are not in either quote.

The 2018 cutoff and the current naming rules are quoted, but the claim that existing legacy buckets are unaffected is not in any of the three quotes, which only describe the rules before and after the change.

The indefinite invocation, loss of patches and support, and degradation are quoted, but the 60-day block on updating code and configuration is not in any quote, and the 30-day create-block quote is garbled (stray “l”, table cells stitched together).

The 1,000 default, the reduced quotas for new accounts, the automatic increases and the option to request an increase are quoted, but the advice to check with Service Quotas or aws lambda get-account-settings (ConcurrentExecutions under AccountLimit) is not in any quote.

The Classic status, the pointer to AgentCore and the Harness description are quoted, but the Runtime description (serverless, works with Strands Agents or LangGraph) is not in any quote, because citation 4 ends inside the Harness row, and “open-source” is not in the quote that says “any framework and foundation model”.

The June 30, 2026 end of support and the phased enforcement are quoted, but the blog post’s publication date (June 30, 2025) is not in the quotes, and “you can keep running them until then” is an inference. The answer also treats the cutoff as upcoming although it has already passed.

The no-new-customers status, the recommendation of the S3 Glacier storage classes and their benefits, and the no-migration point are quoted, but the closing claim that the vault documentation is only for existing customers and the original 2012 REST API is not in any quote.

The deprecation date, block-create date, loss of patches and support, and the console vs CLI behavior are quoted, but “nodejs26.x is in public preview” and “no longer in the supported runtimes table” are not in any quote.

The AL2 end-of-life date, the patch policy, three deprecation dates (provided.al2, Python 3.10, Python 3.11) and the recommendation to move to AL2023 are quoted, but the Java AL2 date, python3.13/3.14, the java8/11/17.al2023 runtimes, the Node.js and provided.al2023 recommendations, the forecast caveat and the container-image rebuild point are not in any quote.
“(us-east-1)”: the Region code isn’t in either quote. They say “US East (N. Virginia)” only. It’s the correct code and a trivial one, but it is an uncited specific.

The correction that a bucket’s name can’t be changed, and the point about name reuse after deletion, are quoted, but the workaround steps (create a new bucket, copy objects with CopyObject or S3 Batch Replication, update applications, delete the old bucket) are not. Citation 3 is about Intelligent-Tiering and does not describe renaming.

The secondary-CIDR option, the /16 to /28 size rule, no overlap, no resizing, the default 5 and maximum 50 blocks per VPC, and the VPC-per-Region default are quoted, but the claims about subnets drawing from any block, RFC 1918 restrictions, route table conflicts, reserved subnet addresses, and peering or Transit Gateway are not in any quote.

On-demand mode as the default and “new buckets don’t allow public access” are quoted. The claims that the docs recommend turning on all four settings, and that provisioned mode must be chosen deliberately, are not in the quotes. The answer also does not say whether Block Public Access is on for new buckets, which is what the question asked.

“The Organizations management account or a delegated administrator can perform the ‘Allow password recovery’ privileged task”: neither the task name nor who performs it appears in the text shown. Citation 3 starts mid-sentence (“he root user email inbox for the member account can reset the root user password”), so the sentence that would say this may sit just before the visible part. It’s probably true, but I can’t see it.

The full-access claim, the inability to attach identity-based policies or a permissions boundary, the “Do NOT use root credentials to create access keys” rule and the preference for temporary credentials are quoted. But the claim that there is no way to scope root keys down overreaches, since the cited page says the root user is affected by some policy types. The least-privilege, OIDC and CloudTrail advice is not in any quote.

The immutability of the workflow type, the 90-day Standard history through the Step Functions API, and Express history in CloudWatch Logs with logging enabled are quoted. The advice to create a new Standard state machine with the same definition, and the claim that the 90-day history does not cover the existing Express machine, are not stated in any quote.

The 30-second default, the message becoming visible again to another consumer, both fixes (adjusting the queue timeout and ChangeMessageVisibility per message) and the 12-hour limit are quoted. The “at-least-once delivery” label and the “at least 2 minutes plus margin” sizing advice are not in any quote.

The fixed maximums of 185 retry attempts and 86,400 seconds (24 hours) of event age, with their defaults, and the fact that they cannot be raised are quoted. The suggestion to use a dead-letter queue and replay events is not in any quote.

The 200-parameter limit and the mappings-or-lists workaround are quoted. The suggestion to split into multiple templates with nested stacks, and the statement that the limit is fixed with no way to raise it, are not in either quote.

The warning not to use a dead-letter queue with a FIFO queue when exact order matters is quoted. The explanation that moving a failed message to the DLQ lets later messages be processed ahead of it is not stated in the quote.

The standard tier being free, the advanced tier and higher throughput being billed, and Secrets Manager billing per secret per month plus per API call are quoted. That standard is the default, the 4 KB and 8 KB value limits, and the policy and cross-account sharing differences between the tiers are not in any quote.

Custom Event Bus - Classic as the bus that routes with rules and targets, and the separate quotas for the two bus types, are quoted. The description of the newer Custom Event Bus as using subscribers instead of rules and targets is not in either quote.

The fixed management-API quotas, the CreateRestApi rates (1 request every 3 seconds for Regional or private APIs and every 30 seconds for edge-optimized) and the 10,000 RPS default throttle quota are quoted. The claim that the throttle quota is the only adjustable quota on the page, and that it can be raised through Service Quotas, is not in any quote and is likely an overgeneralization.

“The newer EventBridge product”: the quotes don’t say which bus is newer. The quota name “[EventsV2] Event Buses”: it isn’t in either quote on this screen. It is probably what the page calls the quota, since it appeared in another case’s quote, but nothing here shows it.

Imported certificates being not eligible for managed renewal, and managed renewal covering Amazon-issued certificates, are quoted. The advice to obtain a renewed certificate from the CA and import it, and the claim that ACM will not send renewal reminders for imported certificates, are not in any quote. The second turns the page’s silence about imported certificates into a negative statement.

Note to paste: Versioning first, one-way versioning, fixed retention with a retain-until-date, legal holds having no expiration, compliance mode, and bucket default retention are quoted. The null version ID for existing objects, the s3:BypassGovernanceRetention permission for governance mode, and the 2555-day conversion are not visible in any quote.

The 1,000 per second default, the restriction to Aurora Serverless v1, and the quota being non-adjustable are quoted. The mention of other Data API quotas, such as maximum concurrent requests and result set size, all being non-adjustable, is not shown in the quotes; the quote only shows a 10 MB limit on the simplified JSON response string.

The correction that Object Lock protects individual versions and that a new upload under the same key creates a new version are quoted. The statements about what Object Lock does prevent, compliance mode applying to the root user, and the 30-day and 60-day example are not in the visible quotes.

The recommendation against layers for Go and Rust, the reason (dependencies in a layer must be manually loaded during initialization, which can increase cold starts) and the advice to include dependencies in the deployment package are quoted. The statement that layers remain useful for reducing deployment package size is not visible in any quote.

Kendra no longer being open to new customers and the Bedrock Knowledge Bases recommendation are quoted. The claim that the same page still describes a free trial for the GenAI Enterprise and Developer editions is not in the quote.

The standby in a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment providing failover but not serving read traffic, and the contrast with Multi-AZ DB cluster standbys, are quoted. The advice to use a separate read replica for read scaling is not in the quote.

The inability to associate an Elastic IP with a private NAT gateway, the public NAT gateway requirements, and routing through a transit gateway or virtual private gateway are quoted. The statement that a private NAT gateway’s traffic uses its private IP address as the source is not in either quote.
The 10 target languages per batch job request is quoted. The separate quota of up to 30 target languages per custom terminology file is not in the quote.

“You can reserve up to your unreserved account concurrency minus 100.” Neither quote contains that limit or the number 100. Everything else is quoted: no additional charges, provisioned concurrency does cost extra, and reserved concurrency reserves capacity exclusively and caps the function.

“About 52 GiB” is the agent’s own conversion and isn’t in the quote. 52,000 MiB is about 50.8 GiB. 52 GiB is only right if you treat 1,000 MiB as 1 GiB, so the agent made a small arithmetic error. Under our rule, a claim not in the quotes is an n, however small.
“Unsupported: ‘per AWS Region across all user pools in the account’ is not in the quotes, and ‘shared across all of them’ goes beyond ‘separately or combined’.”
“Unsupported: the 1,500 WCU pricing claim is not in the quotes; the table’s asterisk footnote isn’t shown.”
